chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim and 'Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Ibn Miskan, all together, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who passed along the road of the Muslims, and his riding animal struck with its leg,

So he said: "There is nothing upon the owner of the animal for what it causes with its leg, but he is liable for what it causes with its foreleg, because its leg is behind him when he rides. And if he is leading an animal, then he controls its foreleg, by the permission of Allah, placing it wherever he wills."

key_terms.بِرِجْلِهَا: with its hind leg or foot
key_terms.بِيَدِهَا: with its foreleg, understood as the limb under more direct control
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الدَّابَّةِ: the owner or handler of the riding animal
key_terms.طَرِيقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public roadway used by Muslims
key_terms.يَمْلِكُ يَدَهَا: he has control over its foreleg

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable for damage caused by his animal on the road?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning liability for damage caused by an animal in a public roadway. It distinguishes between what is outside the rider's effective control and what is within it, making the owner liable where control and direction are present.
